title: Yacht mapper + entity resolution (dedup)
description:
Map parsed yacht table rows into graph nodes and edges, with entity resolution to collapse cross-file duplicates. Yachts (Eclipse, Koru, Dilbar, Azzam...) recur across 5+ files, so dedup on a normalized key of `name + builder + LOA`. For each resolved yacht create a `Yacht` node (attrs: loa, beam, year, value, weekly_rate, guests, cabins, features, location, source_file); create/reuse `Builder` and `Person` (owner) nodes; create `BUILT_BY` (Yacht->Builder) and `OWNED_BY` (Yacht->Person) edges. Merge attributes when the same entity appears in multiple files (prefer non-empty, keep provenance list). Upsert into SQLite via the db helper.

Part of Phase 1 (Ingestion). Entity resolution is the make-or-break of graph quality. Source files: 42, 20, 13, 15, 74.
acceptance_criteria: Yacht rows are deduped on normalized name+builder+LOA so a yacht appearing in multiple source files yields exactly one Yacht node
Merging keeps a provenance list of every source file an entity came from and prefers non-empty attribute values
Builder and Person nodes are created once and reused; BUILT_BY and OWNED_BY edges connect correctly
Re-running ingestion produces the same node/edge counts (idempotent upserts, no duplicate edges)
Unit tests cover dedup (same yacht from two files -> one node) and attribute-merge behavior
